text: Which DNA double-strand break repair pathway uses the sister chromatid as a template and is therefore high-fidelity, in contrast to the error-prone pathway that directly ligates broken ends?
explanation: Homologous recombination repairs double-strand breaks using the sister chromatid as a template, making it high-fidelity, in contrast to non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), which ligates broken ends directly without a template and is error-prone. Mismatch repair corrects replication errors such as base mismatches, and nucleotide excision repair removes bulky adducts like UV lesions -- neither addresses double-strand breaks the way HR/NHEJ do.
